answer: A lock keeper leases one canal lock for 120 days, pays 150 tokens and a 90 dollar fee, and tends its cottage garden. Every boat enters a bound log with time, number, and toll, while a gauge at the chamber nadir records the low water mark after each cycle. A spiral stair is the only access to the gauge, so no reading can be faked from the bank. A forged log forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days; faking 10,000 locks freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A lock is a toll booth filled with water, and a keeper who skips an entry must explain where the water went.
